Krishna lifted a whole mountain on one finger, and held it there for seven days.
Stay till the end, because the real numbers are insane.
Govardhan Hill is about eight kilometres long. Even today, a rough estimate puts it near one hundred billion kilograms.
And that should be impossible. A strong man can deadlift about two hundred kilograms.
An elephant weighs six thousand. A loaded jumbo jet, half a million. The Great Pyramid, six billion.
Govardhan? Around seventeen pyramids. On one fingertip.
But here's the strange part. A fingertip is about one square centimetre. Put that weight on it, and the pressure is around a hundred thousand times what crushes a diamond.
Wait, so how did the hill not crush the finger?
The scriptures say He did it smiling, with His little finger, while the whole village sheltered from Indra's storm.
Because the point was never strength. It was who holds us up when the storm comes.
